newsitem.title: USA: ENSERCH sees problems in Texas proposals.
newsitem.headline: ENSERCH sees problems in Texas proposals.

text.p: Recommendations made to the Texas Railroad Commission by Hearing Examiners would jeopardize the reliability of Lone Star's natural gas service for residential and commercial customers, ENSERCH Corp chief executive David Biegler said.
ENSERCH is the parent company of Lone Star Gas and Lone Star Pipeline.

In a statement released Wednesday following a hearing before the Texas Railroad Commission, Biegler said: "We are concerned that the Examiners would have the Railroad Commission make significant shifts in policy that will ultimately affect the safe and reliable service."
Biegler gave the example of the Hearing Examiners' call for a reduction in the amount of gas available to be delivered from storage for residential and commercial customers.
"About 230,000 of our 1.3 million customers rely on the disallowed storage gas on our coldest days," he commented after his final arguments in a rate case before the commission.
For the first time in 14 years, ENSERCH said, the companies have asked the commission to increase the rate they charge for transporting and storing gas for the 550 cities they serve in Texas.
Instead, the Hearing Examiners proposed applying factors which reduce Lone Star's capacity.

"Without full storage deliverability there is no guarantee that sufficient gas will be available to us," Biegler said. "The company's concern is increased because the Examiners are assessing the customers' need for gas based on an off-peak weather period. We have had to deliver 18 percent more gas for human needs customers that the Examiners have allowed for in their proposal," Biegler added.

Further complicating the concern is a recommendation by the Examiners to place restrictions on gas purchases that would have limited the company's flexibility in purchasing gas to meet reliability requirements while requiring the company to be penalized by $89 million in the test year.
The end result, coupled with other recommendations of the Examiners, would have turned a $39 million profit in the test year to a $50 million loss, Enserch said.
"This is devastating," said Biegler. "The economic survival of Lone Star is at stake."
